text:
Mark Stone became the Golden Knights' all-time leading scorer this week, passing Jonathan Marchessault, and it came during the kind of stretch that makes a milestone feel a little lonely. Vegas is winless in four (0-1-3), the last a shootout loss to Dallas on Thursday, and has been outscored 17-11 in that run.

Don't read much into it. The Knights have had 56% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, in those four games, and 55% on the season. They're 13-6-5, with a 96% chance of making the playoffs and 38% to win the Pacific. If anything, they've scored about five goals fewer than their chances deserve. Adin Hill has been better than his record: .908 on hard shots and 3.8 goals saved above an average goalie over his last five starts, three of them overtime or shootout losses.

The Stone, Jack Eichel and Ivan Barbashev line is back together after a brief experiment ended, and it's won its minutes 10-4. Mitch Marner's line with William Karlsson and Brett Howden is closer to even. Victor Olofsson, in his second stint with Vegas, has 11 points in 10 games, well above the 6.8 his chances point to.

The worry is depth. The fourth line of Nic Dowd, Marc Gatcomb and Braeden Bowman has had a third of the chances and is down 6-1. The Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon pair is also underwater. Those minutes are where one-goal games are being lost.
headline: Stone's record, four straight without a win
